title: ee.daemon.stop.v1
description: Payload schema for the `data` object emitted by `ee daemon stop` (see src/cli/mod.rs::handle_daemon_hot_mode_stop). The outer envelope is the canonical `ee.response.v2` success envelope; this schema describes the inner `data` object only. The SRR1 skeleton (bd-oja31) implements stop as a best-effort unlink of the UDS file; a follow-up slice will add a real shutdown RPC that drains in-flight requests before unlink. The schema is intentionally narrow so future lifecycle fields (e.g. pid, drained_request_count) can be added under a `v2` schema rather than mutating `v1`.

socketPath.description: Absolute path to the Unix-domain socket the stop attempt targeted. Defaults match `ee daemon start` (`${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/ee/daemon.sock` on Linux when the runtime dir is a private per-user directory, otherwise the per-UID `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ee-${uid}/daemon.sock` fallback used on macOS and shared-XDG hosts) and may be overridden via `--socket`. Rendered via `Path::display()`; Unix-only at this revision.

removed.description: `true` when the socket file existed and `fs::remove_file` succeeded; `false` when the socket file did not exist at call time (idempotent no-op). A failed `fs::remove_file` does not emit this envelope at all — the handler returns a `DomainError::Configuration` instead, which surfaces via the canonical `ee.error.v2` envelope. Multi-agent harnesses can therefore treat any successfully emitted `ee.daemon.stop.v1` envelope as 'socket is now absent', regardless of `removed`.
